Add the wine and cook about 10 minutes until absorbed. Add the tomatoes and chile flakes, partly cover and simmer on low 2 1/2 hours, stirring often and adding stock if it threatens to catch.
When thick and the meat is very tender, chop the meat small, return it to the sauce and season.

For the cream sauce, cook the butter and flour on low about 3 minutes without colouring, whisk in the hot milk, bring nearly to a boil, then cook on low about 8 minutes until thick. Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9-by-12-by-3-inch (or 10-by-13-by-3-inch) dish.
Cook the noodles until almost al dente (about 3 minutes for fresh, refreshing them in cold water) and lay them flat on towels.
Layer a thin coat of ragù, then noodles, ragù, cream sauce and Parmesan; repeat, starting and finishing with noodles. Dot with butter.
Bake 45 to 60 minutes until bubbling at the edges, rest 10 minutes and cut into squares.

i: Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling (optional)
1 or 2 juniper berries, crushed in a mortar
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Heat the oven to 350°F. Slice the bread thinly, lay on a tray, drizzle with oil and toast about 5 minutes, just until starting to colour. Cool.
Trim the livers of fat, membrane and any green spots.
Heat the oil in a sauté pan over medium heat, add the livers, prosciutto, tomato sauce and juniper, season and cook 5 to 8 minutes until the livers just firm up, still slightly pink inside.
Cool a few minutes, then lift the mixture onto a board with a slotted spoon and chop to a coarse purée. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve warm in a bowl surrounded by the crostini, or spread on the toasts.

i: 2 ounces thinly sliced prosciutto, cut into 1/4-inch-wide strips
m: Broil the peppers 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until charred all over. Cover in a bowl for about 10 minutes, then peel, seed and dice.
Snap off the woody asparagus ends, peel the stalks up to about 2 inches from the tip and cut on the diagonal into 2-inch pieces.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the asparagus 2 to 3 minutes until tender and lightly browned.
Add the peppers and garlic for about 1 minute, pour in the stock, bring to a boil and take off the heat.
Boil the penne in salted water about 8 minutes, until a little short of al dente, and drain.
Add the pasta and thyme to the skillet over medium heat and cook 5 to 7 minutes, stirring, until al dente.
Mix in the prosciutto, 1/3 cup of the cheese, the remaining butter, salt and pepper.
Serve in a warm bowl topped with the rest of the cheese.

i: 6 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon extra virgin olive oil
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
2/3 pound apple wood–smoked bacon, in a single piece
1/4 pound Roncal, Manchego, or pecorino cheese
m: Heat the oven to 475°F. Halve, seed and peel the squash and cut it into 1/2-inch wedges.
Toss with 4 tablespoons oil, 2 teaspoons salt, pepper and the thyme, spread in one layer and roast about 20 minutes, turning halfway, until tender. Keep warm.
Drop the oven to 375°F and toast the pecans about 10 minutes until fragrant; toss with 1 teaspoon oil and a pinch of salt.
Cut the bacon into 3/8-inch slices, then into 3/8-inch-wide lardons.
Whisk the vinegar with the remaining 2 tablespoons oil and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Put the dandelion greens in a big bowl.
Heat a large pan on high 1 minute and cook the bacon about 5 minutes, until just browning but still chewy. Keep 2 tablespoons fat.
On medium heat stir in the shallots, then take off the heat and swirl in the vinaigrette to warm it.
Add the squash and the bacon mixture to the greens, season with 1/4 teaspoon salt and pepper and toss gently.
Layer half the salad on a platter with half the cheese shaved over and half the pecans; repeat and serve warm.

i: 1 large Vidalia or other sweet onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 red bell peppers, seeded and cut into 1/4-inch dice
1/2 fennel bulb, trimmed and cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 1/2 cups Le Puy lentils or brown lentils, rinsed
Bouquet garni of several fresh thyme sprigs, 1 leek top (optional), and 2 bay leaves, tied in a cheesecloth bundle
2 quarts spring water or chicken stock
1/2 cup Carmenère or other dry red wine
Fruity extra virgin olive oil for serving
Chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley, thyme, or marjoram for garnish
m: Soften the onion, carrots, peppers and fennel in 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium heat, about 10 minutes.
Turn the heat to high, add the garlic and chile and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, bouquet garni and water or stock, salt, bring to a boil and simmer uncovered on medium-low about 45 minutes until very tender.
Meanwhile brown the sausages in the last tablespoon of oil over medium heat 6 to 8 minutes.
Pour in the wine, cover and cook on low about 10 minutes until cooked through.
Discard the bouquet garni, slice the sausages and add them with their pan juices to the soup; adjust seasoning.
Serve very hot with a drizzle of fruity oil and chopped herbs.

i: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Leaves from 1/2 bunch flat-leaf parsley, chopped
1/4 cup loosely packed fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
2 1/2 cups duck stock, chicken stock, or water
1/2 cup clarified butter, melted and cooled
1 1/2 teaspoons ground cinnamon, plus more for sprinkling
12 feuilles de brik or phyllo sheets (see note)
4 teaspoons fresh lemon juice or red wine vinegar
m: Salt the duck legs and brown them in the grape seed oil in a hot heavy pan over medium-high heat, about 5 minutes per side.

In a wide heavy pot, soften the onions in the olive oil over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes. Add the butter, herbs, cinnamon stick, saffron, ginger, turmeric, 1 tablespoon salt and 1 1/2 teaspoons pepper and cook 1 minute.
Lay in the duck skin side up, add the stock, boil, then cover and simmer on medium-low about 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Toast the almonds at 375°F about 10 minutes until golden; cool. Then raise the oven to 400°F.
Lift out the duck and discard the cinnamon stick. Boil the liquid hard until very thick, then on medium-low stir in the eggs about 5 minutes until firmly scrambled. Drain and cool.
Shred the duck meat into bite-size pieces, discarding skin and bones.
Grind the almonds coarsely and mix with the orange blossom water, 1/4 cup clarified butter, sugar and 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, then fold in the duck and eggs.
Keep the pastry covered. Brush one sheet generously with clarified butter, place 1/2 cup filling near the edge, fold over, roll halfway, tuck in the sides and finish rolling. Repeat.
Bake seam side down about 10 minutes until golden; cool 5 minutes.
Dress the arugula with the oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Trim the roll ends, halve each on the diagonal, dust with icing sugar and cinnamon, and stand them around a mound of arugula on each plate.

i: For the Dolcetto wine sauce base:
1 pound salmon bones, rinsed and cut into small pieces
2 1/4 cups Dolcetto or other medium-bodied red wine
To finish the Dolcetto wine sauce:
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into 4 pieces
6 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into 6 pieces
5 ounces chanterelles, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
5 ounces porcini or other wild mushrooms or cremini mushrooms, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch-thick slices or pieces
m: Heat the oven to 450°F. Melt the butter in a roasting pan, toss in the salmon bones and roast about 20 minutes until golden. Remove the bones; lower the oven to 400°F.
On the stovetop over medium heat, caramelize the shallots about 5 minutes, then add the onion, carrot, celery, bay, thyme and peppercorns for 5 to 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and vinegar until the vinegar cooks off, then add the wine and bones and reduce by three-quarters, 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the stock, boil, then simmer uncovered 20 minutes. Strain (about 1 1/2 cups) and keep at a simmer.
For the finish, boil the red wine vinegar almost dry, then the balsamic almost dry, then add the wine and tomato paste and reduce by three-quarters.
Bring both mixtures to a boil and slowly whisk the base into the reduction; simmer on medium about 5 minutes to 1 cup.
Season, whisk in the cold butter piece by piece, strain and keep warm.
Salt the salmon and sear with the halved shallots in the oil in an ovenproof pan over high heat about 3 minutes until golden.
Flip, add the butter, thyme and bay, and roast about 4 minutes for barely translucent (7 for fully opaque).
At the same time, brown the butter in another ovenproof pan, add the mushrooms and sprout leaves, salt, and roast about 5 minutes until tender.
Mound the vegetables on warm plates, spoon sauce around, set the salmon on top, baste with the pan butter and garnish with shallots, thyme and bay.

i: Sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
6 ounces shiitake mushrooms, stems discarded and coarsely chopped
1/2 cup mushroom or vegetable stock, or as needed
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Heat the oven to 425°F. Dry the hens, season, rub with oil and set breast up on a rack in a small roasting pan.
Roast 10 minutes, then lower to 325°F and roast 35 to 45 minutes more until the thigh juices run clear.
For the dressing, sweat the garlic and shallot in the oil over low heat about 5 minutes.
Add the shiitakes on medium heat for 4 to 6 minutes, then the stock, reducing by half, about 2 minutes. Off the heat stir in the soy and lemon juice.
Blend until silky, adding stock to loosen if needed, and season.
Rest the hens 5 minutes, then split each lengthwise.
Toss the greens with 1/4 cup of the dressing. Plate a hen half beside a portion of salad, drizzle the rest of the dressing around, and finish with pepper and cranberries.

i: For the wine and stock reduction:
1 1/2 cups Grenache or other medium-bodied dry red wine
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 pound small cipollini onions (about 1 inch in diameter)
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature
1 tablespoon plus 1 1/2 teaspoons chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 ounces bacon, in a single piece
1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, stemmed and halved
4 tablespoons mixed chopped fresh herbs such as flat-leaf parsley, chervil, tarragon, and chives, in any combination
1 small head frisée, torn into bite-size pieces
m: Sweat the shallots in the butter on low about 5 minutes. Add the wine on high and reduce by three-quarters, about 5 minutes; add the stock and reduce by half, about 10 minutes, until it coats a spoon. Season (about 2 cups).
Brown the cipollini in foaming butter over medium heat about 5 minutes, add the water and cook about 5 minutes more until it evaporates and the onions are tender and browned. Season, cool and halve.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Mash the soft butter with 1 tablespoon parsley, the thyme and garlic, and season.
Loosen the chicken's breast and thigh skin from the cavity end without tearing it, spread the herb butter underneath and season the bird all over.
Toss the potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil and seasoning in a single layer in a roasting pan and set the chicken on top, breast up.
Roast about 1 hour, until a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 160°F.
Cut the bacon into 1/4-inch lardons and fry in a hot pan 3 to 4 minutes until crisp; drain.
Shell the favas, blanch about 30 seconds, cool in cold water and slip off their skins.
Rest the chicken under foil 15 minutes. Toss the potatoes with the remaining parsley and season.
Toss the onions, bacon, favas, tomatoes, herbs and frisée with the last tablespoon of oil and season.
Carve the chicken, serve over the potatoes on a warm platter, with the warmed sauce and the onion salad on the side.

i: 2 tablespoons rendered duck fat or unsalted butter
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
12 cloves garlic, peeled but left whole
8 carrots, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch-thick slices
Bouquet garni of 6 fresh thyme sprigs, 3 fresh rosemary sprigs, 1/2 bunch fresh flat-leaf parsley, and 2 bay leaves, tied in a cheesecloth bundle
m: Heat the oven to 275°F.
Season the shank and brown it well on all sides in the hot duck fat over medium heat, about 10 minutes.
In a deep baking dish or Dutch oven, layer the shallots, garlic, shank, carrots, wine and bouquet garni.
Pour in stock until the ingredients are mostly submerged, with just the top showing, and cover tightly.
Braise 6 hours, until a knife tip slides into the meat with no resistance; if not, give it another 15 to 30 minutes and test again.
Season and serve straight from the dish.

i: For the cabbage, mushrooms, and tuna:
1 head red cabbage, about 1 1/2 pounds, cored, halved, and thinly sliced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/4 cup finely minced, peeled green apple
1 cup Mencía or other dry red wine
3/4 pound cremini mushrooms, trimmed and quartered (about 2 cups)
2 pounds ahi tuna fillets, trimmed of any blood lines and sinew
m: Toast the spice-mix ingredients in a dry pan over low heat 3 to 5 minutes until fragrant, cool and grind finely. Use 1 tablespoon; store the rest.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Toss the cabbage with 1 tablespoon salt and the sugar.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large ovenproof pan on low and cook the bacon about 3 minutes to render.
Add the shallots, garlic and apple for about 5 minutes until soft, then the spice mix for 2 to 3 minutes.
Squeeze the cabbage dry by handfuls into the pan, stir in the wine and vinegar, cover and braise in the oven about 1 hour until soft and the liquid is gone.
Ten minutes before the end, brown butter lightly over medium-high heat, add the mushrooms, season and roast about 5 minutes until tender.
Spread the cabbage in a warm serving dish, top with the mushrooms and keep covered.
Season the tuna and sear in very hot oil over high heat 1 to 2 minutes per side, leaving it rare inside.
Slice across the grain, lay over the vegetables and serve. The cabbage can be made hours ahead and reheated at 350°F for about 15 minutes.

i: 1/2 cup firmly packed dark brown sugar
2 tablespoons unsalted butter or extra virgin olive oil
12 to 16 cipollini or large pearl onions (about 1 inch in diameter), sliced
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Boil the water, pomegranate molasses, sugar, thyme, garlic, pepper and chile paste, stirring, then simmer 5 minutes. Pour into a large bowl and add the ice to cool.
Submerge the turkey thighs, cover and refrigerate at least 3 hours or overnight.
Mix the barbecue sauce ingredients. Soak bamboo skewers about 30 minutes if using.
Drain the turkey, cut the meat off the bone (skin on or off) into rough 1 1/2-inch cubes and thread loosely onto 4 skewers.
Set aside half the sauce for serving and coat the skewers with some of the rest while a grill heats to medium.
For the onions, cover and cook the butter, water, radishes, onions, shallots, sage, salt and pepper over medium heat 10 minutes; uncover on high and cook 3 to 4 minutes until caramelized.
Grill the skewers 8 to 12 minutes, turning often and basting with sauce, until browned and cooked through.
Boil the reserved sauce with the butter and 2 tablespoons wine until thick enough to coat, adding up to 2 tablespoons more wine if needed.
Serve the skewers with the onions, drizzled with some sauce and the rest on the side. No pomegranate molasses? Use 1/4 cup each light molasses and pomegranate juice.

i: 1/4 pound pancetta, in a single piece
1 1/2 cups Nebbiolo or other dry red wine
1 (28-ounce) can San Marzano tomatoes with juice
1 cup polenta, preferably Anson Mills brand
Extra virgin olive oil for serving
m: Salt the duck legs well, cover and refrigerate 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 275°F. Brown the legs skin side down in the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat about 5 minutes, then a minute or two on the other side. Remove.
Cut the pancetta into 1/4-inch lardons. Pour off half the fat and cook the onion and pancetta on medium about 5 minutes, until soft but not crisp.
Add the wine and reduce by half on high, about 5 minutes. Add the hand-crushed tomatoes with juice, the duck and the olives.
Cover and braise in the oven about 1 1/2 hours, until tender but not falling off the bone.
Meanwhile stir the polenta into the water in a heavy 2 1/2-quart pan, salt, and bring to a simmer over medium-high, stirring constantly 5 to 8 minutes until it thickens.
Cook on low, stirring often, about 1 hour until soft. Add the chestnut flour and cook about 10 minutes more; season and keep covered.
Loosen the polenta with hot water if stiff. Serve in warm soup plates topped with a duck leg, sauce and olives, and a good drizzle of oil.
Without chestnut flour, make plain polenta with 1 1/2 cups polenta in total.

i: 1 1/2 teaspoons coarsely ground mixed black and white peppercorns
1/2 pound beef tenderloin or flank steak, in a single piece
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 merguez or other sausages of choice
1 large russet potato, about 4 inches long
m: Whisk the sun-dried tomatoes, garlic and vinegar, then whisk in the oil slowly. Season with the peppercorns and salt.
Blanch the cabbage half in boiling salted water about 3 minutes, chill in cold water, drain, cut into 4 wedges and pat dry.
Heat a grill to medium. Brush the lamb, chicken and beef with oil and season.
Peel the potato and cut into 1/4-inch matchsticks; soak 5 minutes, drain and dry.
Fry in 2 inches of canola oil at 375°F about 8 minutes, stirring, until golden. Drain and keep warm.
Grill, turning once: lamb 3 to 5 minutes a side for medium; chicken 3 to 5 minutes a side until opaque; tenderloin 2 to 3 minutes a side for medium-rare (flank about 4).
Grill the sausages about 8 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Set a cabbage wedge on each plate with greens and a tomato quarter, cut or slice the beef, and arrange all the meats on top.
Top with the fries and pass the vinaigrette. Meats can be grilled an hour ahead and reheated at 350°F for about 5 minutes.

i: 1 bottle (750 ml) Pinotage or other dry red wine
Grated zest and juice of 1/2 orange
1/2 fresh bay leaf or 1 whole dried bay leaf
1 (2 1/2- to 3-pound) boneless pork shoulder roast, rolled and tied
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 pounds carrots (about 10 medium), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch chunks
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 tablespoons nonpareil capers, rinsed and drained
3 tablespoons golden raisins, soaked in hot water to cover for 10 minutes and drained
m: Mix the wine, orange zest and juice, garlic, thyme, bay, cinnamon, juniper and cloves in a nonreactive dish. Add the pork, cover and refrigerate 2 days, turning occasionally.
Heat the oven to 500°F. Lift out the pork (keep the marinade), scrape and dry it, season well and set fat side up in a lightly oiled snug roasting pan.
Roast 30 minutes, then lower to 300°F and roast 2 1/2 to 3 hours until the centre reads 175°F.
Strain the marinade and simmer 30 to 40 minutes until reduced to 1/3 to 1/2 cup.
Brown half the carrots in 2 tablespoons sizzling butter over medium-high heat 4 to 5 minutes until tender (add a splash of water on low if needed). Season, drain and repeat with the rest.
Rest the pork under foil about 15 minutes and skim the fat from the pan juices.
Boil the reduced marinade, pan juices and stock over medium-high heat 10 to 15 minutes to halve. Season, sharpen with vinegar or enrich with butter if you like.
Reheat the carrots in the remaining tablespoon of butter with the capers, raisins and pine nuts; season and add the chives.
Untie and slice the pork and serve with the sauce and carrots.

i: 6 guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded (see note)
4 cloves garlic, peeled but left whole
1/2 small fennel bulb, trimmed and coarsely chopped
1 tablespoon red wine vinegar or other mild vinegar
2 tablespoons fresh tarragon leaves, or 4 fresh tarragon sprigs
m: Bring the beef and water just to a boil in a 5-quart Dutch oven, skimming, then cover and simmer gently on medium-low about 2 hours until nearly cooked.
Remove the beef to cool. Boil the broth uncovered about 15 minutes to reduce to 3 cups, rest 5 minutes and skim off the fat.
Trim the cooled beef of fat and sinew and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Toast the chiles at 350°F about 15 minutes until lightly browned, soak in warm water about 30 minutes, drain and chop.
Simmer the raisins, garlic and fennel in the 3 cups broth, covered, 20 to 30 minutes until soft; cool.
Blend the broth mixture with the chiles, pine nuts, almonds, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth.
Melt the butter in the beef pot over medium-high heat until foaming and brown the beef and prunes about 5 minutes.
Add the sauce carefully (it spits), then cook at a bare simmer uncovered 30 to 40 minutes until the beef is tender, thinning with water if needed.
Serve topped with pine nuts, almonds, tarragon and a pinch of coarse salt. New Mexico red (6) or ancho (4) chiles can stand in for guajillos.

i: 1/2 pound parsnips (2 small), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch chunks (about 1 cup)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 3/4 cups vegetable stock, or as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Simmer the rice and water, covered on low, 17 to 20 minutes until the water is absorbed (about 3 cups cooked).
Cook the seasoned parsnips gently in the oil over medium heat about 10 minutes, without colouring.
Add 1 1/2 cups stock and simmer uncovered 5 to 10 minutes until tender and the liquid has halved. Blend smooth (about 1 cup), adding stock if too thick.
Season the lamb well and sear fat side down in hot oil over medium-high heat 3 to 4 minutes, then about 4 minutes on the other side.
Roast on a tray about 20 minutes for medium-rare, then rest under foil 10 to 15 minutes.
Simmer the cooked rice with the remaining 1 1/4 cups stock, stir in the parsnip purée and heat through; season.
Cut the racks into chops and serve with the rice sprinkled with chives.

i: 4 (3/4-pound) pork rib chops, preferably from pasture-raised pork
For the dried cherry, bacon, and Vidalia onion conserve:
1 1/2 cups Touriga Nacional or other fruity red wine
1/4 pound slab bacon, in a single piece
2 (6-ounce) Vidalia or other sweet onions, thinly sliced
2 tablespoons unsulfured light molasses, or 1/4 cup pomegranate molasses
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 teaspoon aniseeds or fennel seeds, coarsely ground in a mortar or spice grinder
1 teaspoon coriander seeds, coarsely ground in a mortar or spice grinder
m: Trim and dry the chops, rub them with the cut garlic, salt lightly, cover and chill at least 2 hours or overnight. Take out 30 minutes before grilling.
Warm the cherries in the wine to just below a simmer, cool, then drain, keeping cherries and wine separately.
Cut the bacon into 1/4-inch lardons and fry over medium heat 3 to 5 minutes until browned but tender; drain.
Keep 1/4 cup fat in the pan, add the onions and bay leaves for 2 minutes, then cover and cook on very low about 20 minutes until soft.
Add the molasses and vinegar and boil on medium, then add the cherry wine and simmer about 10 minutes until mostly absorbed.
Stir in the bacon and cherries, season with salt and plenty of pepper, and keep warm.
Set up a grill for indirect cooking over medium heat. Mix the ground seeds, pepper and oil and rub over the chops.
Grill over the fire 2 minutes, rotate 90 degrees for 2 more minutes, then move to the cool side, cover and cook 6 to 8 minutes for medium.
Rest under foil 4 to 5 minutes and serve with the warm conserve. The conserve can be made hours ahead; add the bacon at the end.

i: 2 teaspoons dried Greek or other oregano
2 pounds boneless lamb from leg, cut into 1-inch chunks
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Soak bamboo skewers 30 minutes if using.
Mix the garlic, oregano, lemon zest, salt and pepper, then whisk in the oil.
Thread the lamb on the skewers, lay in a dish, coat with the marinade, cover and refrigerate 6 hours to overnight.
For the glaze, brown the shallots in the butter over medium-high heat about 3 minutes, add the wine and boil hard 20 to 30 minutes to a syrup (about 1/3 cup); watch it closely.
Whisk in the honey, salt and some pepper, cook 1 minute and cool. It keeps 2 days chilled; use at room temperature.
Heat a grill to medium and let the lamb come to room temperature.
Shake off the marinade, season, and grill 7 to 8 minutes for medium-rare, turning often.
Near the end brush with the glaze and turn to caramelize it lightly.
Toss the parsley with a squeeze of lemon, the oil, salt and pepper, and pile it over the skewers on a warm platter.
